title: KV quarantine and reshard controller for fragmentation healing
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Introduce a KV quarantine pool and a Reshard Controller that together reduce live fragmentation in the GPU-resident KV cache with minimal impact to tail latency. The quarantine pool holds small, high-churn token slots and clusters them into compact micro-slices. The Reshard Controller continuously monitors occupancy heatmaps, hotness signals, and cost-estimates and issues low-impact relocation/reshard operations during safe windows (low GPU utilization or between batching epochs). Goal: improve usable contiguous space fraction by >= 30% in long-running nodes and cut emergency full compactions by 70% while keeping 95th percentile latency increases < 2%.
acceptance_criteria: Background micro-relocation successfully reclaims small fragmented islands without pausing inference: verified on nightly perf rig
Contiguous free-space metric increases by >= 30% across synthetic long-tail workload replay (72h run)
No user-visible P95 latency regression > 2% when controller is enabled under standard production load
Telemetry exposes fragmentation_ratio, relocation_ops, reclaimed_bytes, and predicted_relocation_cost for alerting
Feature guarded by runtime flag and rolloutable per-cluster in console
design_decisions: Quarantine pool (QP) segregates slots < 64 tokens and with churn_score > threshold to limit scatter from hot prefixes
Reshard Controller uses a cost-benefit model: relocation_gain / relocation_cost >= tunable_threshold to schedule moves
Relocations performed as micro-batches that align with continuous batching epochs to avoid extra GPU kernel launches
Use epochal lease on destination slices to prevent read/write races; KV entries moved with two-phase handoff to maintain correctness
Prefer consolidation into contiguous micro-slices instead of global compaction to bound memory copy work
implementation_notes: Add new KV metadata: churn_score (decay window 10m), frag_token_count, last_touch_ts
QP implemented as lightweight vector of micro-slices with a free-list index encoded in the allocator header
Reshard Controller runs in a dedicated runtime thread; lower priority and backpressure-aware
Relocation uses pinned-page GPU memcpy where available; fallback to device-side copy kernel for NVLink-only nodes
Expose runtime flag redwood.kv.quarantine.enabled and redwood.kv.reshard.rate_limit_ops_per_sec
rollout_plan: Feature behind flag; enable on staging cluster for 48h smoke tests
Canary on 5% of dedicated capacity with slow ramp to 30% while monitoring fragmentation and latency
If alerts for relocation_cost_exceeded or p95_latency_regression fire, automatic rollback to disabled
Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable canary and ops sign-off
telemetry: metrics/kvcache/fragmentation_ratio: ratio of unusable fragmented bytes to total cache bytes
metrics/kvcache/relocation_ops: count of micro-relocations per minute
trace/reshard: trace for each scheduled relocation with pre/post snapshots and cost estimate
testing_plan: Unit tests for churn_score decay, quarantine admission, and two-phase handoff correctness
GPU integration test that simulates continuous batching and ensures relocations coalesce without extra kernel launches
Long-run replay (72h) using mix of synthetic prompt distributions to validate contiguous_free_fraction target
Load test with spike scenarios to ensure relocations back off when headroom is low
Chaos test that kills Reshard Controller mid-operation to verify safety and recovery
